text: Bridgerland Technical College was founded on September 17, 1971.
The college first opened its doors in October of 1971.
Bridgerland began as a vocational center serving Cache, Box Elder, and Rich counties.
In 1984, Bridgerland moved into a building that once made Wurlitzer pianos.
The Logan campus of Bridgerland still sits on the site of that old piano factory.
Bridgerland Technical College has carried four different names since it began.
Bridgerland trains welders, nurses, and machinists right here in Cache Valley.
Bridgerland prepares students for skilled careers without requiring a four year degree.
The Logan campus started out as a Wurlitzer factory that made pianos and electronic organs.
Bridgerland turned the old Wurlitzer factory's assembly lines into classrooms.
Because of its factory roots, Bridgerland's Logan campus is one large building under a single roof.
Before settling in Logan, Bridgerland spent thirteen years moving between spaces like the old Tueller Dance Studio and rooms at Utah State University.
The Brigham City campus later expanded into the former Bourns building.
Bridgerland's Health Sciences building was Utah's top funded project in 2020, lost that funding to COVID, and was refunded in 2021.
Dr. Richard L. Maughan led Bridgerland for 40 years, one of the longest tenures of any Utah college president.
Today, Bridgerland still serves Cache, Box Elder, and Rich counties from campuses in Logan and Brigham City.
Bridgerland runs the only student operated retail meat shop of its kind in the western United States.
Bridgerland's Veterinary Assisting students train hands-on at real veterinary clinics and animal facilities.
Bridgerland's robotics students train on the same brand of industrial robots used across auto and aerospace manufacturing.
Cache Valley stretches across the border between Utah and Idaho.
Shoshone people hunted and fished in Cache Valley long before settlers arrived.
The Northwestern Band of Shoshone called themselves the Pangwiduka, or fish eaters.
Settlers first tried to winter cattle in Cache Valley during 1855.
Peter Maughan founded a lasting settlement in Cache Valley in 1856.
That settlement grew into Wellsville, one of the valley's oldest towns.
Cache County was created by the Utah territorial legislature in 1856.
Fur trappers are said to have cached, or stored, pelts here, giving the valley its name.
Logan was first settled in April of 1859 and named after the nearby Logan River.
Logan was incorporated as a town on January 17, 1866.
Construction on the Logan Tabernacle began in 1865 and finished in 1878.
The territorial legislature established what is now Utah State University in March of 1888.
Box Elder County was separated from Weber County by the legislature in 1856.
Brigham City has served as the seat of Box Elder County since it was founded.
Pioneer William Davis first explored the area near Brigham City in 1850.
The town was first called Box Elder before it was renamed Brigham City in 1877.
On May 10, 1869, workers drove the Golden Spike at Promontory Summit.
That ceremony joined the first transcontinental railroad in America.
Golden Spike National Historical Park now marks that historic meeting point.
Box Elder County stretches from the Great Salt Lake to the Idaho border.
The town of Corinne boomed almost overnight after the transcontinental railroad reached it in 1869.
Corinne was nicknamed the Gentile Capital of Utah during its short lived railroad boom.
The Bear River Migratory Bird Refuge in Box Elder County shelters more than 200 species of birds.
Brigham City has held its Peach Days harvest festival every September since 1904.
Pioneers first entered the Salt Lake Valley on July 24, 1847.
Utah became the 45th state of the United States on January 4, 1896.
The Great Salt Lake is the largest natural lake west of the Mississippi River.
Utah is nicknamed the Beehive State as a symbol of industry and cooperation.
Five national parks lie entirely within the state of Utah.
The Bonneville Salt Flats have hosted land speed racing for over a century.
Salt Lake City has served as Utah's capital since before statehood.
Utah's landscape ranges from red rock desert to snow capped mountains.
